contexts.text: The passion of the cross was the last of the Lord's temptation, through which He fully united the Human to the Divine, and the Divine to the Human...
(Common opinion as to the cross.) AC 7272:2.
These temptations are signified by the cross which they will carry. (.) AC 10490:4. AC 10490:7.
All things done by the Jews to the Lord when He was crucified, signified the states of their Church as to Divine truth, or the Word.
The cross was the last of His temptations... and after it He put on Divine good, and thus united His Divine Human to the Divine itself which was in Him.
That by this last combat, which was the passion of the cross, He fully subjugated the Hells, the Lord teaches in .
He wanted to preach the Lord crucified...
The passion of the cross was the last combat or temptation, through which He fully conquered the Hells, and fully glorified His Human. DLord 12, General article.
Through the passion of the cross, the Lord did not take away sins, but carried them. General article.
Their crucifying Him = that they had destroyed and profaned the whole Word. TCR 130:3. AE 122:4.
The full unition of the Divine and the Human in Him was effected through the passion of the cross, which was the last of His temptations. General article.
That he should take up his cross () = that he should fight against concupiscences. AE 934:end.
The cross = temptation. Illustrated. AR 639:2, Illustrated. AE 893:3, Illustrated.
The reason that nation was permitted to crucify the Lord. Explained.
Where also our Lord was crucified () = no acknowledgement of the Lord's Divine Human, and thus a state of rejection. AE 655.
He who loves evils, also loves to do evil to the Lord, nay, to crucify Him: this is inmostly latent in all evil...
The Divine truth of the Word teaches that those who for its sake afflict their souls and crucify their flesh, shall have peace in the Lord. Signified.

In the celestial sense, to commit murder means to be rashly angry with the Lord, to hate Him, and to will to blot out His name: these are they of whom it is said that they crucify Him; which also they would do... if He were to come into the world as before.
Under Baptism, see these references. TCR 685:end.
Man must receive Him, but not as He hung on the cross...
(When the Spirit formed a cross with the bright stings, he excited the nearest ones.)
He said he sat at the wood (of the Lord's cross).
The sign of the cross seen on a lofty mountain: an indication that Babylon was recommenced.
To carry the cross () = to undergo assaults and temptations by falsities.
Under Blood, see this reference.
The Lord's despair on the cross. Explained.
The Jews crucifying the Lord = that the evils and consequent falsities which they loved crucified Him.

What crucifixion, or hanging upon wood, signified among the Jews... There were two death punishments among them; crucifixion and stoning; and by crucifixion was signified condemnation and a curse on account of the destruction of good in the Church... The reason was, that the wood upon which they were hung = good, and, in the opposite sense, evil.

That hanging upon wood, or crucifixion, was imposed on account of the destruction of good in the Church, and that it thus represented evil from infernal love, from which come condemnation and a curse. Illustrated.
To crucify () relates to the good of doctrine... and = to destroy.
The cross = man's proprium, against which he is to fight.

The Jews said to me, Why did Christ suffer the cross? I replied, Because He was the greatest Prophet, and therefore carried the iniquities of the people, as the prophet who lay on his right side... of whom it is also said that he carried the iniquities. In like manner other prophets... When they heard this, they said that they would go away and consult together.
